label: Weight Loss
tagline: 80% diet, 20% exercise — let's focus on what you eat
description: A moderate calorie deficit paired with higher protein and fiber to keep you full while you lose fat, not muscle. primaryTargets.calorieDeficit is a positive number of calories below your TDEE (500 = eat 500 fewer calories/day than maintenance).
coachingTips: Protein and fiber are your best friends for staying full on fewer calories.
Bulky, low-calorie-density foods like vegetables let you eat a large volume without blowing your budget.
A slow, steady deficit beats a crash diet — aim for consistency, not perfection.
Watch liquid calories: sugary drinks and juices add up fast without filling you up.

label: Hair & Skin Health
description: Calories stay at maintenance (TDEE) — this goal is about nutrient quality, not quantity. Focuses on the vitamins, minerals, and healthy fats most linked to hair growth, skin elasticity, and a healthy complexion.
coachingTips: Omega-3s from fatty fish and nuts help keep skin supple and support scalp health.
Vitamin C helps your body build collagen — pair it with iron-rich foods to boost absorption.
Biotin-rich foods like eggs, salmon, nuts, and seeds support hair strength and growth.
Hydration matters as much as nutrients — don't forget your water intake.

label: Muscle Gain
tagline: Fuel the build — eat to grow
description: A calorie surplus to support muscle growth alongside training. primaryTargets.calorieDeficit uses the same sign convention as Weight Loss but negative: -250 means a 250 calorie surplus above your TDEE. Protein multiplier stays at 1.0g per lb bodyweight, but on top of a surplus this yields a higher absolute protein target than the same multiplier during a deficit.
coachingTips: Spread protein evenly across meals instead of loading it all at dinner.
Zinc and magnesium both support the hormonal side of muscle recovery and growth.
A surplus doesn't mean unlimited junk — favor nutrient-dense calories over empty ones.
Track consistently: small, steady surpluses build muscle with less added fat than big ones.

label: Energy & Focus
tagline: Steady fuel for a sharp mind
description: Calories stay at maintenance (TDEE). Prioritizes the nutrients most tied to steady energy levels and mental clarity, while capping sugar to avoid energy crashes.
coachingTips: Low iron is one of the most common hidden causes of fatigue — prioritize iron-rich foods.
Complex carbs with fiber release energy more steadily than refined sugar.
B-vitamins (B6, B12, folate) are essential for converting food into usable energy.
Sugar spikes feel good for 20 minutes and cost you the next two hours — favor whole foods.

label: Bone Health
description: Calories stay at maintenance (TDEE). Prioritizes calcium and its key cofactors — vitamin D, vitamin K, magnesium, and phosphorus — which all work together for bone density and strength.
coachingTips: Calcium needs vitamin D to be absorbed well — pair dairy or leafy greens with some sun or fortified foods.
Magnesium and phosphorus are often overlooked but are just as important as calcium for bone density.
Weight-bearing movement plus these nutrients does more for bone strength than diet alone.
Leafy greens like spinach and broccoli offer both calcium and vitamin K in one food.

label: Gut Health
description: Calories stay at maintenance (TDEE). Pushes fiber intake higher than the other goals (30g+) since fiber feeds beneficial gut bacteria, and caps sugar since excess sugar can disrupt gut flora balance.
coachingTips: Fiber is fuel for your gut microbiome — aim for a variety of plant sources, not just one.
Excess added sugar can feed less-friendly gut bacteria — keep it in check.
Fermented foods and fiber-rich vegetables are a great everyday combination.
Introduce more fiber gradually and drink plenty of water to avoid digestive discomfort.

label: Overall Wellness
tagline: Hit all your bases every day
description: The default goal, used when a user hasn't selected a specific focus. Calories stay at maintenance (TDEE) with balanced macro targets. priorityNutrients is intentionally left empty here: rather than a fixed nutrient list, the real behavior is to dynamically sort all tracked nutrients by whichever the user is furthest short of that day — that sorting logic lives in the log-engine layer, not in this data file.
coachingTips: Balance beats extremes — a variety of whole foods covers more nutrient bases than any single 'superfood'.
Pick a specific goal above if you want more targeted coaching for weight, muscle, energy, or a specific health focus.
Small, consistent habits compound into big results over months, not days.
Check your daily nutrient breakdown to spot which areas need the most attention.
